blocks.content: The President appoints the Chairman and other members of the Commission by warrant under his hand and seal.

Subject to conditions prescribed in the parent Act

items: Although the Governor appoints members of the State Public Service Commission (SPSC), only the President of India has the power to remove them.
Selection committees for statutory appointments typically comprise the Prime Minister, the Speaker of Lok Sabha, and the Leader of Opposition.
UPSC members cannot be re-appointed for a second term in the same position to safeguard administrative integrity and independence.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Members of Constitutional Bodies such as the UPSC and Election Commission are appointed directly by the President of India.
Qualifications for appointment are generally specified in the Constitution or prescribed by Parliament through relevant enabling legislation.
The tenure of members is protected to ensure autonomy, usually fixed at 6 years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Members of statutory bodies like the NHRC and CIC are appointed on the recommendations of a designated high-powered selection committee.
Members of major constitutional bodies are rendered ineligible for further employment under the Central or State Governments upon demitting office.
